# PSX company research framework — v1

Recovered on 2026-09-09 from the user's “PSX Research Organization” conversation (6aa12670-1700-83e9-a95d-593bdf19457d), specifically the later, more detailed system proposal accepted in that discussion. The earlier six-category score is superseded here by the later seven-category model. Detailed scoring anchors below are our implementation, not a claim that the user supplied them.

## Dossier coverage

A. Business, segments, owners, management, competitive position.
B. Industry structure, peers, growth drivers, regulation and cyclicality.
C. At least five annual periods: revenue or sector-equivalent income, profit, EPS, returns, balance sheet, cash flow, margins.
D. Earnings quality: core earnings versus gains, provisions, cash flow, dilution and accounting changes.
E. Dividends: history, payout, sustainability and growth.
F. Governance: audit, related parties, capital allocation and execution.
G. Catalysts with observable evidence and review triggers.
H. Risk register, then sector-appropriate valuation, bear/base/bull, thesis, verdict, confidence and missing information.

## Score weights

| Category | Maximum |
|---|---:|
| Business quality | 20 |
| Financial strength | 20 |
| Growth | 15 |
| Management | 10 |
| Dividend quality | 10 |
| Valuation | 15 |
| Risk (higher means more resilient) | 10 |

85–100 Exceptional; 75–84 Strong; 65–74 Good / Watch; 55–64 Average; below 55 Weak / Avoid. These labels do not determine a purchase decision.

Implementation: score each category against the available evidence, explain deductions, and label subjective scores provisional. As a working anchor, about 90% of available points requires strong evidence with few material unresolved weaknesses, about 70% indicates strengths offset by meaningful weaknesses, and about 50% indicates mixed or weak evidence. Use null for unassessed categories; do not silently give missing data zero or normalize an incomplete score to 100. Keep confidence separate from score. This is not a backtested ranking model.

## Sector adaptations

For banks use net spread and total operating income, ROE/ROA, capital adequacy, CET1, liquidity, deposit mix and asset quality. Deposits are operating funding: conventional corporate debt/EBITDA, gross margin, ROIC and OCF-minus-capex dividend coverage are generally unsuitable. Analyze cash flows but do not call deposit inflows shareholder free cash flow. Value with P/E, P/B alongside sustainable ROE, and dividend scenarios. Separate consolidated and standalone series.

Other sectors: E&P uses reserves and production plus earnings and cash flow; cement uses EV/ton and EV/EBITDA with replacement cost; technology emphasizes growth, earnings and FCF. Never force bank methods onto non-banks.

## Evidence and maintenance

Prefer PSX filings, company financial statements, regulatory documents, briefings, then secondary sources. Mark facts, calculations, management claims and assumptions. Every dataset records period, units, basis, source and locator. Keep financial period, publication date, retrieval date and quote timestamp separate. Save reports, validated page-marked text and SHA-256 checksums. Reuse local extracts before rereading full PDFs; inspect pages when columns or scanned text are ambiguous.

Use companies/<TICKER>/ for one persistent dossier per company; shared templates and skill live outside the company folder. Preserve dated history before updating current conclusions. Refresh sources and prices on each update, describe what changed and flag stale fields. Portfolio sizing and execution remain separate from research.

# Focused PSX SIP portfolio — 10 September 2026

## Purpose

Build toward a long-term, Shariah-compliant Pakistani equity portfolio of seven companies using Rs 100,000 each month. This is a research-led allocation framework, not a guarantee of returns or a request to sell everything currently held.

## Current position

The CDC statement dated 9 September 2026 reports a portfolio value of Rs 788,743 across 21 holdings. It does not provide cost bases, so unrealised profit/loss cannot be assessed.

MEBL is the dominant holding: 615 shares times the PSX quote of Rs 556.12 on 9 September is about Rs 342,000, or about 43% of the reported total. Its existing weight is already above the long-term target below. New MEBL purchases should therefore be paused while the rest of the portfolio catches up.

Lalpir Power (LPL) was classified non-compliant in the PSX KMI All Share recomposition effective 5 June 2026. Do not add new money to it. Consult the investor's preferred Shariah adviser on the appropriate treatment of existing shares and any purification calculation.

## The proposed seven-company destination portfolio

| Ticker | Role | Target weight | Why it is here | Main watch item |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| MEBL | Islamic banking | 15% | High-quality deposit franchise, capital and asset quality; full dossier completed. | Sovereign exposure, expense growth and sustainable earnings. |
| LUCK | Industrial / cement | 15% | Scaled cement business with earnings growth and diversification. | Cement cycle, energy costs and group capital allocation. |
| MARI | Energy / E&P | 15% | Strong earnings and balance sheet; energy exposure diversifies domestic demand risk. | Production, reserve replacement, pricing and state-policy risk. |
| SYS | Technology / exports | 15% | Export-oriented technology exposure and a different source of growth. | Latest standalone profit softness; review consolidated cash generation. |
| FFC | Fertilizer / income | 15% | Established fertilizer franchise and income contribution. | Recent Sharia income ratio was 4.97%, very close to the 5% screen; reconfirm at each review. |
| HALEON | Consumer health | 12.5% | Defensive consumer-health brands and low screen debt. | Weak consumer demand and margin pressure. |
| COLG | Consumer staples | 12.5% | Everyday consumer-products exposure, distinct from the cyclical sectors above. | High valuation, low free float and pricing-volume balance. |

The targets are for the eventual selected basket, not instructions to force the current account to those levels immediately. No holding should exceed 20% through new purchases.

## Monthly SIP transition

For the next six months, direct the full Rs 100,000 only to names below their target weights after marking the account at current prices. Start with this provisional monthly split, then recalculate quarterly:

| Ticker | Monthly amount | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| MEBL | Rs 0 | Already about 43% of the account. |
| LUCK | Rs 20,000 | Existing position is small. |
| MARI | Rs 15,000 | Existing position is meaningful but below the proposed target. |
| SYS | Rs 15,000 | Existing position is below target; buy only after the consolidated-results check. |
| FFC | Rs 20,000 | Opens the fertilizer/income position; recheck Sharia status before each semiannual review. |
| HALEON | Rs 15,000 | Builds consumer-health exposure gradually. |
| COLG | Rs 15,000 | Builds staples exposure gradually. |

This is a *contribution* plan. It does not call for selling your current positions. If prices did not move and no sales occurred, MEBL would fall from about 43% to about 25% of the portfolio after six months of these contributions, and toward 17% after twelve months. Actual results will differ because prices, dividends and other holdings change.

## Why FFC instead of EFERT for new money

Both pass the latest PSX Shariah screen. EFERT's reported FY2025 profit fell versus FY2024 and its Q2 2026 profit was weaker year on year. FFC's latest results were more resilient, so FFC is the tentative new-money choice. Keep the existing EFERT shares, collect evidence, and choose only one fertilizer company for recurring additions.

## What must be checked before the first purchase

1. Confirm the latest PSX Shariah status for every purchase. The cited screen uses financial statements at 31 December 2025; status can change.
2. Read the latest consolidated results for SYS, and the latest full annual reports for the six companies without a completed dossier. A screen is not complete fundamental research.
3. Confirm the account's cost basis, dividends received and cash balance. The supplied statement has quantities and market value only.
4. Keep an emergency reserve outside equities. This plan assumes the monthly Rs 100,000 is money that can stay invested through a 30–40% market decline.

## Review rule for a low-maintenance investor

Review after every half-year result and after each PSX Shariah recomposition. Add only to the most underweight 2–3 approved names that month. Pause a company when Shariah status changes, leverage rises materially, the dividend is cut for operational reasons, or the original business thesis breaks.

## Sources

- CDC Account Balance Report, 9 September 2026 (local supplied document).
- PSX, *Recomposition of PSX-KMI All Share Islamic Index*, notice PSX/N-659, 29 May 2026; effective 5 June 2026. It shows the classifications and underlying December 2025 screening ratios.
- PSX company pages and published financial statements for MEBL, LUCK, MARI, SYS, EFERT, FFC and HALEON, accessed 9 September 2026.
- Colgate-Palmolive Pakistan, financial reports page, accessed 9 September 2026.

## Research status

MEBL has a full local dossier. The other six are a screened shortlist, not yet full dossiers. The next research cycle should create the same annual-report, interim-report, valuation and risk files for LUCK, MARI, SYS, FFC, HALEON and COLG before increasing their allocation above this initial transition plan.

# Meezan Bank Limited — PSX: MEBL

**Initial research | 9 September 2026 | Verdict: Watch | Provisional score: 74/100**

Meezan has a strong deposit franchise, low reported problem financing and substantial capital buffers. Its earnings are recovering from the 2025 decline, but the first-half 2026 improvement is less convincing underneath: costs grew much faster than income, pre-provision profit fell, and almost all the increase in standalone profit after tax came arithmetically from the lower tax charge. At the observed price of **Rs 556.12**, the shares already command a premium to the selected bank peers. The moderate valuation scenario offers little price upside. Business assessment confidence is **medium**; valuation confidence is **low to medium**.

This is an initial dossier under the recovered [PSX framework](../../FRAMEWORK.md), with explicit gaps rather than a claim of exhaustive due diligence. Financial figures below are **unconsolidated/standalone**, except the separately labeled group comparison. Amounts are **PKR billion** unless marked otherwise. H1 means January–June; annual figures are calendar years. Calculations use reported figures and can differ slightly from rounded tables.

## Latest evidence and source map

The latest annual report located is for **31 December 2025**. The latest financial period located is **30 June 2026**. PSX lists the half-year results announcement on **6 August 2026**, report transmission on **25 August**, and dividend-credit notice on **2 September**. The share quote is timestamped **9 September 2026, 3:49 PM Pakistan time**. These dates refer to different events. [PSX company page](https://dps.psx.com.pk/company/MEBL)

Five original PDFs are archived with page-marked text and checksums in [sources.json](sources.json):

| ID | Source | Main locators used |
|---|---|---|
| A25 | [Annual report 2025](https://www.meezanbank.com/wp-content/themes/mbl/downloads/annualreport2025.pdf) · [local PDF](reports/annual-2025.pdf) | Printed pp36–42, 80; PDF pp187–188 audit; printed pp194, 196, 245–247, 264 |
| H26 | [Half-year report 2026](https://www.meezanbank.com/wp-content/themes/mbl/downloads/HYjune2026.pdf) · [local PDF](reports/interim-H1-2026.pdf) | Printed pp4–7, 12–18, notes 5.1.2, 23, 24, 38–40; p53 group P&L |
| B26 | [June 2026 analyst briefing](https://www.meezanbank.com/wp-content/themes/mbl/downloads/Analyst-Briefing-Jun2026.pdf) · [local PDF](reports/briefing-H1-2026.pdf) | Slides 8–15 |
| A24 | [Annual report 2024](https://www.meezanbank.com/wp-content/themes/mbl/downloads/annualreport2024.pdf) · [local PDF](reports/annual-2024.pdf) | Archived comparative source; not separately audited by this research |
| H25 | [Half-year report 2025](https://www.meezanbank.com/wp-content/themes/mbl/downloads/HYjune2025.pdf) · [local PDF](reports/interim-H1-2025.pdf) | Archived comparative source; H1 comparisons below use H26's comparative columns |

References such as “A25 p80” mean the printed page; this corresponds to PDF page 82. H26 printed p14 corresponds to PDF page 15. Page numbers in extracted text are explicitly **PDF page numbers, one-based**. Bank and PSX versions may have different cover/transmission pages; do not assume equal pagination or identical bytes.

## A. Company and competitive position

Meezan takes deposits and deploys funds through Islamic financing, investments and placements, while earning fees from payments, cards, trade and other banking services. Subsidiaries include Al Meezan Investment Management and Meezan Exchange Company. The income mix is increasingly investment-heavy: H1 2026 gross returns comprised **Rs 146.55bn from investments**, **Rs 75.88bn from financing**, and **Rs 0.35bn from placements**. Investments therefore generated about **66%** of gross returns. These are income-source categories, not a substitute for a complete segment-profitability analysis. [H26 notes 1, 24 and 38]

At June 2026 it operated **1,150 branches in 372 cities**. Current accounts were about **49%** of deposits and current plus savings accounts (CASA) about **91%**. Its briefing reported a **9.1% share of banking deposits**; this is management's figure and has not been reconciled here to SBP industry tables. A large current-account base is valuable because it gives the bank access to low-cost funding. Savings accounts still carry a return cost, so 91% CASA does not mean 91% free funding. [H26 p6; B26 slides 14–15]

The largest disclosed shareholders at December 2025 were Noor Financial Investment **35.03%**, Pakistan Kuwait Investment **29.82%**, and Islamic Development Bank **9.27%**: together **74.12%**. Ownership supports a stable sponsor base but concentrates voting control. Dr. Syed Amir Ali is the CEO and Riyadh S. A. A. Edrees the chairman in the latest half-year corporate information. [A25 note 23.3, p245; H26 p3]

## B. Industry and business drivers

Competition comes from Islamic banks and Islamic operations of conventional banks. UBL and Bank AL Habib are useful listed valuation references, although their business mix is not identical. Deposit growth, access to government Sukuk, digital customer acquisition and demand for Islamic products can support expansion. The bank reports one third of H1 new customers were onboarded digitally. Whether that lowers long-term cost per customer remains to be demonstrated in subsequent expenses. [H26 pp6–7]

Rates affect both asset returns and payments to depositors. Management attributes the 2025 earnings decline partly to lower policy rates and minimum deposit-return requirements for Islamic banks. H1 average policy rates were also below the prior-year average, despite an increase during the period. These are management's period explanations, not a fresh verification of the current SBP policy stance or the exact regulatory rule. [A25 p36; H26 pp4,6]

## C. Five-year financial record

| Standalone metric | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Net spread | 68.92 | 121.70 | 226.43 | 287.04 | 252.47 |
| Total operating income | 83.81 | 140.81 | 248.54 | 315.92 | 285.10 |
| Operating and other expenses | 35.32 | 48.25 | 71.79 | 84.61 | 86.80 |
| Profit before provisions | 48.49 | 92.56 | 176.75 | 231.31 | 198.30 |
| Profit after tax | 28.36 | 45.01 | 84.48 | 101.51 | 89.04 |
| Basic EPS, Rs | 15.84 | 25.15 | 47.18 | 56.62 | 49.54 |
| Deposits | 1,455.89 | 1,658.49 | 2,217.47 | 2,584.87 | 3,302.84 |
| Total assets | 1,902.97 | 2,577.40 | 3,012.11 | 3,902.07 | 4,806.56 |
| Gross financing | 777.30 | 1,018.10 | 992.03 | 1,556.36 | 1,686.27 |
| Equity | 86.56 | 115.32 | 184.91 | 246.98 | 279.26 |
| ROE, % | 36.4 | 44.59 | 56.27 | 47.01 | 33.84 |
| ROA, % | 1.7 | 2.01 | 3.02 | 2.94 | 2.04 |
| Capital adequacy, % | 17.8 | 18.42 | 22.39 | 20.35 | 19.20 |

Source: A25 printed p80, visually checked because extraction duplicated some columns. [Machine-readable annual data](data/annual-financials.csv) includes more metrics. Historical EPS is as presented in the bank's comparative summary; raw historical DPS below is not bonus-adjusted. The bank notes that comparative figures can be rearranged or restated, and IFRS 9 adoption introduces comparability limitations.

Profit grew at about **33.1% annually from 2021 to 2025** and deposits at **22.7%**, calculated across four annual intervals. That impressive history includes unusually high-return years. In 2025, profit fell **12.3%**, net spread fell **12.0%**, and ROE declined to **33.84%**. Deposit growth alone does not guarantee profit growth.

### Latest half-year comparison

| Standalone metric | H1 2025 | H1 2026 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net spread | 125.756 | 128.786 | +2.4% |
| Fee and commission income | 10.873 | 13.512 | +24.3% |
| Total other income | 15.923 | 21.626 | +35.8% |
| Total income | 141.679 | 150.412 | +6.2% |
| Operating and other expenses | 35.858 | 45.257 | +26.2% |
| Profit before provisions | 105.821 | 105.155 | −0.6% |
| Net credit-loss charge | 3.379 | 2.604 | −22.9% |
| Profit before tax | 102.442 | 102.551 | +0.1% |
| Tax charge | 56.278 | 53.671 | −4.6% |
| Profit after tax | 46.164 | 48.880 | +5.9% |
| Basic EPS, Rs | 25.72 | 27.15 | +5.6% |

Source: H26 printed p14, visually checked; [interim data](data/interim-financials.csv).

At June 2026, deposits rose **13.1% from December** to **Rs 3.735tn**, investments rose **11.8%** to **Rs 2.903tn**, and gross financing fell **2.9%** to **Rs 1.638tn**. Financing was nevertheless up about **38% versus June 2025**; the comparison date changes the story. The gross financing/deposit ratio fell from **51.1% to 43.8%** since December. [H26 p5; B26 slide 12]

## D. Earnings quality and balance-sheet resilience

**The tax bridge matters.** Standalone PAT rose Rs 2.716bn. PBT increased only Rs 0.109bn; the tax charge decreased Rs 2.607bn. Thus about **96% of the PAT increase is arithmetically explained by lower tax expense**. This does not establish a one-off tax benefit: the underlying tax reconciliation still needs deeper review. Lower provisions also offset declining pre-provision earnings. [H26 p14; calculated]

**Costs are the key operating test.** Cost/income increased from about **25.3% to 30.1%** year on year. Management cites branch expansion, staff, IT, inflation and customer-servicing costs. Strong fees help, but a sustained cost growth rate above income growth would pressure earnings. Q2 PAT improved about 9% from Q1, but sequential growth alone does not resolve the weak year-on-year pre-tax result. [H26 p6; B26 slides 8–10]

**The group headline is different.** Consolidated H1 PAT was **Rs 48.641bn**, up **3.2%** from Rs 47.140bn. Profit attributable to parent shareholders was **Rs 48.100bn**, up **3.2%** from Rs 46.604bn; consolidated EPS rose from **Rs 25.97 to Rs 26.71**. Standalone dividend income can include intra-group distributions that are eliminated on consolidation. A full consolidation bridge is outstanding; neither series should be silently substituted for the other. [H26 p53]

**Reported asset quality and capital are supportive.** June non-performing financing was about **Rs 29.9bn**, the NPF ratio **1.83%**, and coverage **152%**. CAR was **19.22%**, CET1 **17.40%**, LCR **266%**, and NSFR **205%**. LCR fell from 314% at December, although reported liquidity remains substantial. These are reported ratios, not a stress test. The 2025 directors' report cites an 11.5% minimum CAR for that year; current institution-specific buffers have not been independently refreshed. [B26 slide 8; H26 note 39, p49; A25 p42]

**Sovereign exposure and market values matter.** The annual report says sovereign/government-guaranteed securities represented about **99% of the 2025 investment portfolio**. June total investments are roughly **56.5% of assets**. Revaluation surplus/deficit fell from **+Rs 14.380bn to −Rs 0.042bn** in H1. Equity grew only about 3.4% despite retained earnings. Government-backed assets can still produce rate-sensitive valuation losses and concentrated country exposure. [A25 p38; B26 slide 12]

**Cash flow is positive, but not industrial-company FCF.** Operating cash inflow was **Rs 881.296bn in 2025**, against Rs 361.233bn in 2024; H1 2026 was **Rs 388.787bn**, against Rs 607.655bn. Deposits and interbank funding materially drive these flows. They cannot be treated as cash freely available to shareholders. Dividend resilience depends more on recurring earnings, capital, liquidity and asset quality. Five-year OCF extraction is incomplete and marked blank for 2021–2023. [A25 p194; H26 p18]

**Accounting caveat.** A25 note 3.5 states that full IFRS 9 revenue recognition would have reduced 2025 gross return by Rs 4.514bn and tax by Rs 2.392bn, a net Rs 2.122bn earnings difference. H26 note 5.1.2 shows the opposite period direction: return would have been Rs 1.703bn higher and tax Rs 0.886bn higher, net Rs 0.817bn. These are disclosed counterfactuals under local reporting differences, not adjustments made to this dossier's reported EPS. Also distinguish the directors' Rs 9.1bn financing allowance charge from the **Rs 3.886bn total net P&L provision charge** in 2025; they are different measures. [A25 pp39,80,196; H26 p22]

## E. Dividend record and sustainability

| Year/period | Cash dividend per share, Rs | Basic EPS, Rs | Approximate payout |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2021 | 6.00 | 15.84 | Not compared on mixed bonus-adjustment bases |
| 2022 | 8.50 | 25.15 | Not compared on mixed bonus-adjustment bases |
| 2023 | 20.00 | 47.18 | 42.4% |
| 2024 | 28.00 | 56.62 | 49.5% |
| 2025 | 28.00 | 49.54 | 56.5% |
| H1 2026 | 15.50 | 27.15 | 57.1% |

A25 p80 reports cash dividends as percentages of Rs 10 face value; the table converts these to rupees. Bonus issues were 15% in 2021 and 10% in 2022; earlier DPS is the contemporaneous unadjusted amount, so this is not a total-return series. H1 2026 comprises **Rs 7.50 for Q1 plus Rs 8 for Q2**, as disclosed in the directors' review. [A25 p80; H26 p5]

At Rs 556.12, the **2025 dividend yield is 5.03%**. Doubling H1 DPS to Rs 31 gives **5.57%**, but that is an annualization assumption, not a declared full-year dividend. Payout around 57% leaves earnings for capital growth; this is supportive, conditional on earnings quality and regulatory requirements. The period's cash-flow dividend payment differs from the period's declared dividend because payment dates differ.

## F. Governance and audit

A.F. Ferguson's 2025 standalone audit opinion is unmodified under the accounting and reporting standards applicable in Pakistan. The key audit matter reviewed concerns expected credit losses on Islamic financing and off-balance-sheet obligations, emphasizing estimation and judgment. The opinion and the first key-audit-matter pages were visually inspected; the scanned audit section is absent from text extraction. H1 accounts have a limited review, and the auditor explicitly excludes a review of the standalone Q2-only figures. [A25 PDF pp187–188; H26 p12]

Related-party dealings include subsidiaries, associated funds, directors and key personnel. The bank states these occur on substantially comparable terms; that is a management assertion, not our independent confirmation. Sponsor concentration, related-party balances, remuneration and historical delivery against guidance merit a fuller governance review. [A25 note 47, pp264 onward; H26 note 38]

Unprovided tax contingencies of **Rs 1.802bn** relate to specified HSBC acquisition-related disputes; management expects favorable outcomes. Total contingencies and commitments were **Rs 2.067tn** at June, mainly ordinary banking commitments and guarantees. That total is not a forecast loss or immediately payable debt. [H26 note 23, p38]

## G. Catalysts and H. risk register

| Item | Assessment | What to monitor |
|---|---|---|
| Deposit and fee expansion | Positive catalyst | Retain low-cost deposit mix and fee growth without proportionate cost expansion |
| Productivity from digital investment | Potential catalyst | Cost/income and pre-provision profit improve across subsequent comparable quarters |
| Financing recovery | Potential catalyst | Growth deploys liquidity profitably without worse NPF or capital ratios |
| Rates and deposit remuneration | High earnings sensitivity | Repricing of asset yields and funding costs; fresh SBP rules |
| Sovereign concentration and OCI | High structural exposure | Investment mix, duration, fair-value reserve, liquidity and capital effects |
| Tax/regulatory changes | High | Effective tax reconciliation, enacted rules, court outcomes; do not extrapolate tax-led growth |
| Cost expansion | Medium–high | Expense growth falls below income growth; branches mature |
| Credit deterioration | Medium | NPF, stage-2 migration, collateral assumptions, sector concentration and coverage |
| Governance/dilution | Medium | Related-party exposures and share issuance; issued shares exceed the June base on PSX |

Severity is qualitative analyst judgment, not an estimated probability. Evidence: A25 and H26 sections cited above. No dates or earnings benefit are assigned to unconfirmed catalysts.

## Valuation and historical context

The observed price implies approximately **10.91×** a simple standalone TTM EPS of **Rs 50.97** (49.54 − 25.72 + 27.15). PSX displays **10.94×**. The small mismatch remains unreconciled; weighted share counts and rounding can make summed EPS differ from a platform's methodology. This dossier preserves both values. [PSX MEBL](https://dps.psx.com.pk/company/MEBL); A25 p80; H26 p14

June book value is approximately **Rs 160.32 per share**, using Rs 288.656bn equity / **1,800,554,652 June issued shares**. The price is **3.47× this dated book value**. PSX now shows **1,807,096,448 shares**; June equity should not silently be paired with a later share count. Subsequent issuance and dividend effects need a book-value roll-forward before calling this a current P/B. [H26 balance sheet and note 39; A25 note 23.2; PSX]

| Peer snapshot, 9 September 2026 | Price, Rs | PSX-displayed standalone TTM P/E |
|---|---:|---:|
| [MEBL](https://dps.psx.com.pk/company/MEBL) | 556.12 | 10.94× |
| [UBL](https://dps.psx.com.pk/company/UBL) | 426.07 | 7.16× |
| [BAHL](https://dps.psx.com.pk/company/BAHL) | 155.85 | 6.76× |

MEBL's displayed P/E is about 53% above UBL and 62% above BAHL. This is a screening comparison, not proof of overvaluation: business mix, ROE, risk, one-offs and growth are not yet normalized. Peer quotes were timestamped 3:49 PM for UBL and 3:48 PM for BAHL; BAHL was marked ex-dividend.

A25 p80 shows year-end P/E of **8.46, 3.96, 3.42, 4.27 and 8.97×** in 2021–2025, and year-end P/B of **2.50, 1.54, 1.56, 1.76 and 2.87×**. Today's multiples exceed these year-end observations. These five points are not a full historical distribution, and the unusually high earnings of 2023–2024 depressed their P/Es.

### Provisional scenarios, not an adopted price target

| Scenario | Annual EPS assumption | P/E assumption | Indicated value | Price upside/downside | Implied P/B on June book |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bear | Rs 45 | 8× | Rs 360 | −35.3% | 2.25× |
| Base | Rs 54 | 10× | Rs 540 | −2.9% | 3.37× |
| Bull | Rs 60 | 12× | Rs 720 | +29.5% | 4.49× |

Formula: annual EPS × selected P/E. Base EPS is close to doubling H1 EPS (Rs 54.30), conditional on no material seasonality or deterioration. Bear assumes renewed margin/cost pressure; bull assumes stronger underlying earnings. The 8× bear multiple retains some premium over the screened peers; 10× base is near the current multiple; 12× bull requires renewed investor willingness to pay a higher premium. These are transparent analyst assumptions, not consensus estimates or multiples derived from a calibrated regression.

The P/B column is an implied cross-check, not an independent second valuation. A sustainable-ROE residual-income/dividend model is still needed. No scenario probabilities are assigned. Price upside excludes dividends, tax and trading costs. The broad Rs 360–720 range illustrates sensitivity; **Rs 540 is a provisional base scenario, not a verified intrinsic value**. The machine-readable adopted fair value remains null. [Model inputs and formulas](data/valuation.json)

## Provisional score

| Category | Score | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Business quality | 18/20 | Strong deposit franchise; concentrated domestic exposure |
| Financial strength | 17/20 | Capital and reported credit quality; sovereign/OCI risks remain |
| Growth | 10/15 | Deposit growth strong; underlying earnings weaker |
| Management | 7/10 | Reporting and distributions supportive; deeper governance review open |
| Dividend quality | 9/10 | Consistent payouts and about 57% current payout |
| Valuation | 6/15 | Premium multiples; limited base-case upside |
| Risk | 7/10 | Buffers help; country, rate, tax and execution risks persist |
| **Total** | **74/100** | **Good / Watch under the framework** |

This is a subjective initial score with explicit deductions, not a backtested quantitative assessment. Outstanding evidence reduces confidence. It should not automatically dictate a trade.

## What would change the view?

A stronger case would require sustained growth in pre-provision earnings, lower relative cost growth, stable asset quality and a better-supported valuation margin. A weaker case would be rising impaired financing, worsening capital/liquidity, continued tax-led rather than operating growth, or a higher price without improved earnings.

Next review: **September 2026 results when published**, or an earlier material regulatory/company announcement. See [prioritized open questions](OPEN_QUESTIONS.md). No monitoring schedule has been activated. This research is separate from portfolio allocation and trade execution.
